els.text: Bordeaux's famous sweet wine, from grapes touched by noble rot. Honey, apricot and orange marmalade. Classic with blue cheese, especially Roquefort.
Fermented in concrete eggs and old French oak for a rounder, creamier Kiwi Sauvignon. Fresh herbs, gooseberry, passionfruit and lime.
Estate-grown Chardonnay from the Cordoni family, who make wine in the hills of Umbria and keep a second home in Knoxville, Tennessee.
Pinot Noir (Pinot Nero in Italian) from the Cordoni family's small estate in Montone, Umbria, where they grow their own grapes.
From a small family winery in the green hills of Montone, Umbria. The Cordonis grow their own grapes and make just a handful of artisan wines.
One of Beaujolais' ten crus, from the steep slopes of Mont Brouilly and its hard blue stone. Dark berries, a little pepper and a mineral edge.
Organic, unoaked Garnacha from central Spain. Ripe cherry and red berries with a peppery, violet-scented finish. Easy with charcuterie.
Grower Champagne from a family estate in Avize, in the Côte des Blancs, founded in 1920. All Grand Cru Chardonnay: chalky, mineral and lightly toasty.
Spain's under-the-radar native red, grown inland between Valencia and La Mancha. Deep color with black cherry, plum and a little spice.
Jaffurs is best known for Rhône-style wines; this is their Santa Barbara County Pinot. Cherry, sage and orange peel over black tea and spice.
Russell Joyce's whole-cluster Gamay from a cool, windy corner of Monterey. Light and juicy, with sour cherry, cranberry, strawberry and herbs.
From Kopke, the oldest Port house, founded in 1638. Aged in oak casks: dried fruit, toasted nuts, caramel and spice. Lovely with blue cheese.
From Jorge Ordóñez, who helped introduce Albariño to America. Old vines in Rías Baixas give stone fruit, citrus and pear with a salty finish.
País came to Chile with Spanish missionaries in the 1500s. Rafael Tirado makes it light and lively: blood orange, red cherry and herbs.
South Africa's own grape, a 1925 cross of Pinot Noir and Cinsault, made here in an elegant style. Raspberry, cedar and a whiff of rosemary.
Savoie's native red grape: light on its feet, with dark berries, violets and a peppery kick. A natural with Beaufort and other Alpine cheeses.
Côte des Bar, Champagne  ·  Pinot Noir
A Rosé de Cuvaison: all Pinot Noir, given a short soak on the skins for its color. Rose petal, crushed red berries and kirsch.
From a small family estate in Breedekloof, made by winemaker Elizma Visser. Lime, grapefruit and nectarine with a hint of honey and chamomile.
From a seventh-generation family estate in the Slanghoek Valley. Light and juicy, somewhere between a rosé and a red. Serve it a little cool.
Grown around the Étang de Thau, a saltwater lagoon famous for its oysters. Zesty lemon, green apple and a salty snap. The name means “lip stinger.”
From Ridgecrest, the first vineyard on Oregon's Ribbon Ridge, planted by Harry Peterson-Nedry in 1980. Pear, peach and citrus with crisp acidity.
From the Thaya winery near Znojmo, by the Dyje (Thaya) River and the Austrian border. Crisp and herbal, with green apple and pear.
A Cabernet-led Bordeaux blend from the cool lower slopes of the Helderberg, by Longridge winemaker Jasper Raats. Red berries, cherry and bay leaf.
The Basque coast's own white: lighter in alcohol, with a gentle spritz. Citrus, stone fruit and a salty, mineral snap. Pour it from up high.
An Aussie take on Piedmont's grapes, named for Barolo's truffle hunters and their dogs. Cherry, herbs and a savory, amaro-like finish.
From Master of Wine Amy Christine, co-owner of Holus Bolus in Santa Barbara County. A California red built on Malbec and Mourvèdre.
